tabGroups_description.message: Automatically sorts tabs that aren't in a group of your own into 9 groups (today, yesterday, … last year) by when they were opened or — an option in Settings — when they were last used, and moves them on after midnight. In Settings you can also add groups from bookmarks: tabs bookmarked in a chosen folder (optionally also any address on the bookmark's domain) get a group of their own. Automatic groups stay to the right of your own groups, from oldest to newest.

tabGroups_intro_opened.message: Tabs outside your own groups are sorted into groups automatically by when they were opened.

tabGroups_intro_last_used.message: Tabs outside your own groups are sorted into groups automatically by when they were last used.

tabGroups_intro_opened_bookmarks.message: Tabs outside your own groups are sorted into groups automatically by when they were opened, and bookmarked tabs in the chosen folders into groups from bookmarks.

tabGroups_intro_last_used_bookmarks.message: Tabs outside your own groups are sorted into groups automatically by when they were last used, and bookmarked tabs in the chosen folders into groups from bookmarks.

tabGroups_unsupported.message: This browser doesn't let extensions manage tab groups (Chrome 89+, Firefox 139+ on desktop).

tabGroups_missing_permission.message: Tab groups permission is missing — nothing is being sorted yet.

tabGroups_missing_alarms.message: Without the alarms permission, groups move on after midnight only the next time you work with tabs.

tabGroups_missing_bookmarks.message: Groups from bookmarks need access to bookmarks and tab addresses — they aren't used yet.

tabGroups_permission_floating.message: It can't be granted from the floating window — allow it in the popup, side panel or Settings.

tabGroups_overview_in_sandbox.message: The overview of the window's groups with "Regroup now" and "Identify managed groups" is Tab Groups Sandbox — by default in the popup.

tabGroups_bookmarks_describe_domain.message: on the domains of bookmarks in the "$1" folder
